why: Zigzag order is level-order traversal (BFS one level at a time) where every other level's list is reversed before it is recorded.
hints: First get plain level order: BFS, processing exactly len(queue) nodes per round.
Keep a flag that flips each level. When it says right-to-left, reverse that level's values.
Always enqueue children left then right; only the recorded list is reversed. O(n) time, O(width) space.
pitfalls: Do not reverse the order you enqueue children in; that scrambles deeper levels.
statement:
Given the root of a binary tree, return its node values level by level. Level 0 (the root) is read left to right, level 1 right to left, level 2 left to right, and so on, alternating. Missing children produce no entries. An empty tree gives [].

Worked example. Tree [1,2,3,4,null,null,5]: root 1 with children 2 and 3; 2 has left child 4; 3 has right child 5.

  • Level 0, left to right: [1].
  • Level 1 holds 2, 3; read right to left: [3, 2].
  • Level 2 holds 4, 5; read left to right: [4, 5].
  • Answer: [[1], [3, 2], [4, 5]].
constraints:
• Bounds not stated in the source; reasonable ones for practice:
  • 0 <= number of nodes <= 2000
  • -100 <= node.val <= 100
